$comment: GOLDEN CONTRACT — the 'must not change' Airtable surface the three Airtable-as-source-of-truth skills depend on. DERIVED from the skill reference docs (managing-inventory/references/airtable-schema.md, building-decks/SKILL.md + strategy-schema.md, chasing-cards/SKILL.md). This is the Phase-0 baseline: if any table/field named here disappears or a write op path breaks, the happy-path workflow has regressed. Tables and fields are addressed by NAME (not per-base tbl…/fld… ids): names are stable across bases while ids are per-base, so the harness resolves the live tbl… ids by NAME at runtime via the Airtable meta API. The base id is likewise env-driven (AIRTABLE_BASE_ID) with a turnkey default, so a different Airtable instance can run this suite without editing the contract.

Inventory Cards.$derived_comment: CARD-DIM / ENGINE-DERIVED classification (#5). These Inventory Cards columns are a PURE FUNCTION of the card's Scryfall identity (keyed to oracle_id), so the pipeline's card-dim write-back OWNS them: they are engine-writable, NOT human-authoritative — even though the skills READ them. This partitions the Cards fields: everything in required_fields that is NOT listed here stays human/collection-authoritative (the write-back denylist), and these derived fields join the ⚙ Buckets / ⚙ Otags allowlist. The regression harness still checks each of these exists on the live table (they remain in required_fields); this list only reclassifies write-authority. Disjoint by construction from #6's owned-facts write surface (Card Name / Number Owned / Foil Count / Condition / Sets / Sources).

Chase Cards.$derived_comment: CARD-DIM / ENGINE-DERIVED classification (#5, 5b-3, #5 otag extension). The live Chase Cards table now carries the SAME ELEVEN engine-derived columns as Inventory Cards (verified against the live base tblXsNtGgT7UQLPXZ): the nine Scryfall-pure columns PLUS the two engine ⚙ otag fields (⚙ Buckets / ⚙ Otags), which were just added to the live Chase table to match Inventory. The pipeline's chase card-dim write-back OWNS exactly these eleven — they are engine-writable, NOT human-authoritative — even though the skills READ them. ASYMMETRY vs Inventory: Inventory's inline write emits only its nine Scryfall columns (its ⚙ fields come from the separate otag SYNC path), whereas Chase has NO otag sync, so the chase INLINE write is the ONLY path to ⚙ on Chase — which is why the two ⚙ fields are listed in the chase derived_fields here (emitted by the chase payload builder), not just on the allowlist. Everything in the chase skills' required_fields that is NOT listed here stays human/collection-authoritative (the chase write-back denylist: Card Name / Sets / Target Decks); the live table's further human/system fields (Trades (In)/(Out), Is Land/Creature/Non-Creature, Created At, Price Last Updated, Created, Last Modified) are not on the allowlist and so are refused by the closed-set guard regardless. Mirrors the Inventory 'derived_fields' structure so the chase derived-vs-human split is single-homed in the contract.

scratch_write.$comment: Table the --full round-trip creates/updates/deletes a clearly-marked scratch record in. Chase Cards is chosen because it is a leaf table with no inbound links from human-edited records, a plain text primary field, and its own delete path exercised by chasing-cards. The round-trip NEVER touches Inventory Cards/Decks/Trades where a stray record could pollute deck formulas. The table is addressed by NAME; the harness resolves its live tbl… id at runtime.
